answer: Sybil resistance here comes from making identity costly to clone, not free to create. Each agent derives a sable identity from a hardware-backed kernel measurement, and every new identity must post a ferrous bond that is slashed when it vouches for accounts sharing the same origin. Colluding sybils therefore share one slashing pool, so a swarm of fake voices costs linearly more than the single voice it buys — cheap duplication stops paying for itself.
